name: Recording indicator dot
plain: A green or orange dot shows when an app is using the camera or microphone.
meaning: System drawn, so apps cannot hide it. Android also adds hardware toggles that cut access.

android.prompt_ui: Green dot with chip, camera and microphone toggles in Quick Settings
android.note: Indicator shown for camera and microphone; Android 14 adds location indicator

ios.prompt_ui: Orange dot for microphone, green for camera, Control Center shows app
ios.note: Dot can't be hidden by apps; iOS 14 also shows source app in Control Center

limits.headline: Can't use the camera or mic without a green or orange dot showing
limits.user_action: Nothing. The dot shows by itself when the camera or mic is in use
can: Show a green dot for the camera and an orange dot for the mic
Show the app name in Control Center (iPhone)
Show a chip with toggles in Quick Settings (Android)
cannot: Show on older phones before iOS 14 or Android 12
Show a location indicator with this dot; Android 14 adds one separately
limits.differs: Android 12 and later has a chip and toggles, and Android 14 adds location. iPhone (iOS 14 and later) uses dots.

story.what_it_is: A system drawn green or orange dot that shows when an app uses the camera or mic.

marketing.name: Privacy features
marketing.pitch: The recording indicator shows when an app has access to your camera or microphone.

marketing.name: Privacy indicators
marketing.pitch: Android shows icons in the status bar when apps use the camera or mic.

story.for_you: You see a dot that apps cannot hide. Control Center or the chip tells you which app is using the sensor, so you can check and shut it off.
story.for_makers: Because the system draws it, makers cannot disguise sensor use. Teams plan features so that the camera or mic starts only when the person clearly expects it.

use_cases.example: A call app lights the dot when you join and stops when you leave.
A voice chat game keeps the mic indicator only during talk.
A short video app shows the dot while you film.
A user spots a flashlight app using the mic and deletes it.
A screen reader announces the dot so a blind user knows a sensor is on.
An IT team teaches staff to check the dot during sensitive meetings.

risks: Does not show where data goes
story.android_note: Android also adds hardware toggles on some phones that cut access.
story.ios_note: iOS draws the dot above all apps in the status area.

technical_bounds: Cannot be turned off by apps
